OpenPipelines is open-source. Whether you want to fix a typo, report a bug, or add
a whole new workflow, contributions are welcome.

## Ways to contribute

You don't have to write code to help.

- **Report a bug or request a feature.** Open an issue on the relevant package
  repository (see [Set up your environment](getting-started.qmd) for the list).
- **Improve the documentation.** Documentation for arguments, components, workflows, and these guides can always be improved.
  If you spot something wrong or missing, open an issue or a pull request.
- **Contribute code.** Add a [component](creating-components.qmd) or [pipeline](creating-pipelines.qmd), or fix an existing one.
  See the steps below for more details on this process.

## Making code contributions

Contributing code to an OpenPipelines package follows these steps:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-contributing-flow
%%| fig-cap: "The code contribution process"
%%{init: {"theme":"base", "themeVariables":{"fontSize":"14px"}}}%%
graph LR
    classDef step fill:#eaf5e6,stroke:#b3d99e,color:#000

    Fork["<b>Fork & clone</b>"]:::step
    Develop["<b>Develop locally</b>"]:::step
    Test["<b>Test</b>"]:::step
    PR["<b>Pull request</b>"]:::step
    Review["<b>Review</b>"]:::step
    Merge["<b>Merge</b>"]:::step
    Publish["<b>Publish</b>"]:::step

    Fork --> Develop --> Test --> PR --> Review --> Merge --> Publish
```

Start by forking the package you want to contribute to and creating a new development branch.
Develop your change locally, using Viash to build and test components.
When the change is ready, open a pull request against the `main` branch of the package repository.
A maintainer will review it and provide feedback.
When everything is ready, the branch will be merged and the changes included in the next release published on Viash Hub.
These pages provide more detail on the different steps.

:::{#contributing}
:::

## Where to get help

Stuck? Open an issue on the package repository, or start a discussion on
[GitHub](https://github.com/openpipelines-bio). Questions are welcome, including
"is this the right place for my change?" before you start.

## Code of conduct

OpenPipelines adopts the
[Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/). We pledge to keep
the community welcoming, inclusive, and harassment-free, and by taking part you
agree to uphold it. Please read the full
[Code of Conduct](https://github.com/openpipelines-bio/openpipeline/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
before participating.
